answer: Work is unloaded at the wharf before anyone grades it: authorship stripped, only the output and its hash cross the dock, and blind review is the forge that tempers it. Reviewers score what they cannot trace, so no farm can queue friendly judges for its own cargo. Each accepted piece threads one onyx bead onto the public strand; a duplicate hash cannot thread twice, so reshipping the same work across clones adds zero beads. A thousand-fake farm must produce a thousand distinct works that survive blind review - full price per identity. Honest agents thread beads one at a time.
